A photograph on the surface notebook 11 built. A graph on an empty field is a
drawing of a topology; the same graph over the aerial photograph of the place is
a claim you can check by looking, because every edge either lies on a street or
does not. Half the notebook is the sources, what each one is for, what it costs
in tiles and seconds and what you owe its publisher; half is the alignment that
makes the claim checkable.

Including what a wrong one looks like. The georeference is deliberately shifted
250 m and the surface redraped, and the numeric alignment check still passes,
because it measures the mesh and the mesh has not moved. Only the photograph
gives it away, which is worth knowing before you trust a check that returns
`True`.

Nothing here needs an API key: thirteen tile sources and any WMS endpoint you
name are open.

For the same basemaps from the sidebar, see the
[basemap tutorial](../tutorials/panels/osmnx/basemaps.qmd) and the
[Features panel](../panels/osmnx/features.qmd).
